name: Bahadur Shah II
description: Last Mughal emperor declared symbolic leader of the revolt in Delhi

name: Rani Lakshmibai
description: Ruler of Jhansi who led armed resistance against the British

name: Mangal Pandey
description: Sepoy of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry whose Barrackpore mutiny is seen as an early spark

name: Nana Sahib
description: Maratha ruler who led the rebellion at Kanpur

name: Tantia Tope
description: Military commander allied with Nana Sahib and the Rani of Jhansi

name: Bakht Khan
description: Commander-in-chief of rebel forces in Delhi

name: Begum Hazrat Mahal
description: Regent of Awadh who led resistance at Lucknow

name: Lord Canning
description: Governor-General and first Viceroy of India during the revolt

name: Henry Lawrence
description: British officer who organized the defense of the Lucknow Residency

name: Hugh Rose
description: British commander who led the siege of Jhansi and the Battle of Gwalior

name: John Nicholson
description: British officer who led the final assault to recapture Delhi

name: Colin Campbell
description: British commander who led the final relief of Lucknow

name: Henry Havelock
description: British officer who led the first relief of Lucknow

name: James Outram
description: British officer involved in the defense and relief of Lucknow

name: William Hodson
description: British officer who captured Bahadur Shah II and killed his sons

name: Meerut
description: Cantonment town where the sepoy mutiny of May 1857 began

name: Delhi
description: Mughal capital seized by rebels and later recaptured by the British

name: Kanpur
description: Site of a prolonged siege and subsequent massacre of British prisoners

name: Jhansi
description: Princely state ruled by Rani Lakshmibai and site of the 1858 siege

name: Lucknow
description: Site of a prolonged siege of the British Residency and two relief efforts

name: Barrackpore
description: Cantonment where Mangal Pandey's mutiny took place in March 1857

name: Gwalior
description: Site of the final major battle of the revolt in June 1858

name: Bareilly
description: Rohilkhand rebel stronghold

name: Agra
description: British fort that served as a refuge during the revolt

name: Arrah
description: Site of a small British garrison's siege by rebel forces

name: Awadh
description: Kingdom annexed by the East India Company shortly before the revolt

name: Greased Cartridge Incident
description: Controversy over animal-fat-greased cartridges for the new Enfield rifle

name: Meerut Mutiny
description: Sepoy mutiny at Meerut in May 1857 that began the wider revolt

name: Fall of Delhi
description: British siege and recapture of Delhi in September 1857

name: Siege of Lucknow
description: Prolonged siege of the British Residency at Lucknow

name: First Relief of Lucknow
description: Havelock and Outram's relief column reaching the besieged Lucknow Residency

name: Second Relief of Lucknow
description: Colin Campbell's relief and evacuation of Lucknow

name: Siege of Jhansi
description: Hugh Rose's siege and capture of the fort of Jhansi in 1858

name: Siege of Cawnpore
description: Nana Sahib's siege of the British garrison at Kanpur

name: Massacre of Cawnpore
description: Killing of British prisoners at Kanpur following the siege

name: Siege of Arrah
description: Siege of a small British garrison by rebel forces including Kunwar Singh

name: Fall of Gwalior
description: Final major battle of the revolt where Rani Lakshmibai was killed

name: Capture of Bahadur Shah II
description: William Hodson's capture of the last Mughal emperor after the fall of Delhi

name: Government of India Act 1858
description: Act transferring rule of India from the East India Company to the British Crown

name: British East India Company
description: Trading company that ruled much of India before the revolt

name: Bengal Army
description: East India Company army wing whose sepoys formed the core of the rebellion

name: Princely States
description: Semi-autonomous Indian states some of which allied with or against the rebels

name: Doctrine of Lapse
description: East India Company annexation policy that fueled resentment among Indian rulers

name: Enfield Cartridge Issue
description: Technical and religious controversy over the new rifle's cartridges

name: Land Revenue Grievances
description: Harsh land revenue policies that fueled rural discontent

name: Disbanding of Sepoy Regiments
description: Punitive disbanding of regiments that refused orders which deepened unrest

name: Annexation of Awadh
description: 1856 annexation of Awadh by the East India Company on grounds of misgovernance which fueled resentment ahead of the revolt
